title: Pre-Loop Setup and Loop-Body Duplication
pattern: Repeating sequential initialization logic immediately before a loop and duplicating it at the end of the loop body.
why_bad: A developer making subsequent modifications might change one block of statements but neglect to update the other, introducing state synchronization errors.
detection: A sequential block of statements preceding a loop that is textually identical to the final statements of that loop.
counterexample: Buffering mechanisms where the initial priming read explicitly requires different validation logic from steady-state sequential reads.
source: *Code Complete* (2nd Edition), Chapter 22: "C++ Example of Duplicated Code That Will Break Down Under Maintenance", p. 573.
